subject: EdgeBurst Dedicated: Concurrency profile + prompt taxonomy request
messages:
From: Naomi Feldman <naomi@redwood.com>
To: Alex Park <alex.park@edgeburst.ai>
Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa@redwood.com>, Karthik Iyer <karthik@redwood.com>
Date: Sat, 11 Jul 2026 09:12:00 -0700
Subject: EdgeBurst Dedicated: Concurrency profile + prompt taxonomy request

Hi Alex —

Thanks for the call today. To get the Dedicated sizing team comfortable with the commit, could you fill out the quick signature/profile below so we can produce a concrete GPU mix and burst quota recommendation? We need realistic samples rather than hand-wavy averages. The attached CSV is an example format.

Requested items (short answers ok):
1) Representative request rate: typical RPS and observed peak RPS (15m window) over the last 30 days.
2) Prompt taxonomy: percent split by prompt type (short intents <50 tokens, form-filling 50-200 tokens, long-context >200 tokens).
3) Average response length (tokens) and 95th percentile response length.
4) Session behavior: % of requests using session/KV cache and average KV cache hit rate.
5) Expected concurrency per user session and typical session duration.
6) SLO targets (p50/p95/p99 latency targets) and tolerance for async/batch fallbacks.
7) Any heavy multimodal/embedding usage that needs separate GPU SKUs.
8) Peak days and timezone where the peak concentrates (helpful for scheduling burst capacity).

If you can paste the small CSV back or attach an export from your telemetry, we’ll run a quick projection and map to a recommended reserved pool (GPU type mix, baseline commit, burst quota, and an expected cost per 1M tokens).

We’ll also point out where caching or prompt re-write could reduce unit cost by ~20–40% in many cases.

Thanks — Naomi
Naomi Feldman
SENIOR SOLUTIONS ENGINEER, REDWOOD INFERENCE
naomi@redwood.com | +1 (415) 555-0182

Attachment: edgeburst-workload-sample.csv (CSV, 42 KB)
From: Alex Park <alex.park@edgeburst.ai>
To: Naomi Feldman <naomi@redwood.com>
Cc: contracts@edgeburst.ai
Date: Mon, 13 Jul 2026 08:04:00 -0700
Subject: Re: EdgeBurst Dedicated: Concurrency profile + prompt taxonomy request

Naomi —

Appreciate the clear checklist. I attached a sanitized telemetry export and filled the CSV. High level answers inline here:

1) Typical: 18 RPS sustained, Peak (15m): 420 RPS (we saw a couple of spikes during product launches).
2) Prompt taxonomy (approx): short intents 55%, form-fill 30%, long-context 15%.
3) Avg response length: 68 tokens. 95th pct: 410 tokens (rare multi-turn summarizations).
4) ~45% of requests use session KV; estimated KV hit rate 62% on those sessions.
5) Concurrency-per-session: typically 1–3 concurrent requests; session duration 2–12 minutes depending on flow.
6) SLOs: p95 < 300 ms for short intents; p95 < 900 ms for long-context; p99 can be relaxed to 2.5s for bulk operations. Can accept queued async fallback for >5s.
7) We occasionally call embeddings for reranking (small batch jobs), about 5% of traffic — probably separate.
8) Peaks: Product release events every ~4–6 weeks, concentrated in US-Eastern business hours.

I flagged some rows in the CSV where we sampled token distributions. Happy to hop on a second call if you need more granularity.

— Alex
Alex Park
Head of Platform, EdgeBurst
alex.park@edgeburst.ai | +1 (646) 555-1390

Attachments: token-distribution-snapshot.xlsx (XLSX, 120 KB)
From: Naomi Feldman <naomi@redwood.com>
To: Alex Park <alex.park@edgeburst.ai>
Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa@redwood.com>, Karthik Iyer <karthik@redwood.com>
Date: Mon, 13 Jul 2026 10:02:00 -0700
Subject: Re: EdgeBurst Dedicated: Concurrency profile + prompt taxonomy request

Alex —

This is great, thank you. Quick notes from the sizing team after a first pass on your CSV:
- With 420RPS 15m peak and the token mix you provided, our baseline projection points to a dedicated pool of 4x A100-80GB-equivalent GPUs with a 2.5x burst bucket for release-day spikes (we’ll provide a concrete cost delta).
- Because ~15% of traffic is long-context and those requests dominate KV memory and decoding time, we’ll propose a mix: 2 GPUs tuned for long-context (higher memory), 2 GPUs optimized for high-throughput short responses (throughput kernels / quantized paths).
- KV cache utilization at ~62% is good — enabling prefix caching aggressively on the long-context pool reduces per-token GPU time by ~18% in our benchmarks.
- We recommend a canary rollout: start with 50% traffic to Dedicated during a non-peak day, measure p95 and token econ, then ramp.

Action items for us (Marissa & Karthik): create the cost & throughput slide for the commit tier, propose burst SLAs, and add an autoscale smoothing window tuned for your release-day patterns.

Can you confirm whether EdgeBurst requires tenant isolation (separate VPC/Private deployment) or if dedicated shared-tenant pools are acceptable? Also confirm whether embedding jobs should be routed to a separate reserved pool or run on burst capacity.

We’ll get the draft recommendation to you by EOD Wednesday.

Best — Naomi
From: Alex Park <alex.park@edgeburst.ai>
To: Naomi Feldman <naomi@redwood.com>
Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa@redwood.com>, Karthik Iyer <karthik@redwood.com>, contracts@edgeburst.ai
Date: Tue, 13 Jul 2026 16:45:00 -0700
Subject: Re: EdgeBurst Dedicated: Concurrency profile + prompt taxonomy request

Naomi / team —

Confirming: we need tenant isolation for regulatory reasons (separate VPC) and embeddings should have a small reserved pool (1 GPU) with burst allowed into the main pool. Also please include a suggested SLA credit matrix for missed p95s during the first 90 days of the pilot.

If you can include a sample mutual action plan in the Deck (dates, telemetry gating criteria, signoff owners), we’ll attach it to the purchase order.

I’ll send a redacted SOC-2 addendum to contracts after we get the draft.

Thanks — Alex
